races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with relevant placed form over 13–15f on Soft and Firm; carries headgear (hood-going-p), is 8 years old but in fair recent nick off just 8 days, and holds the race-shape advantage with Mr Henry Main (3lb claim) ensuring light enough handling to sustain the lead.
runners_data.comment: Consistent front-runner type who has finished second, second, and third in her last three starts, Sea Of Charm arrives here just eight days on from her latest effort and has experience of today's distance and going — winless in recent starts, but her level of consistency makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Best recent form in the field with a win and four places over 12f on Good, making him the most credible hold-up threat; trainer Gihan Arnolda has 0 from 2 in the past 14 days, and at 4 years old he has scope, but his style requires a contested pace that may not materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Highland Harvey has solid claims on recent form, placed in four of his last six starts including a win three starts back, and he handles today's distance and going; the concern is that his 150 lb burden could blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with six placings from recent runs over 12f on Good and Standard, making her natural position just off the pace ideal for this shape; T14 figures of 2/7 show reasonable trainer form, though the 26-day absence and lack of a win in this sample temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Stintino Sunset has been a model of consistency, placing in five of her last six starts, and having run over today's trip and going she arrives with relevant experience and a speed rating that edges above her official mark — the worry is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: 9-year-old hold-up performer fitted with tongue-strap (hg: tp), returning after just 8 days; recent history over shorter trips (8–10f) raises a distance stamina query at 1m4f, and sim-going figures of 0W3P on comparable surfaces suggest honest but limited upside.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Wrist Art looks up against it here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and was placed two starts back, at least suggesting some residual ability.

runners_data.name: Little She
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a tongue-strap (hg: t) who has placed at 12f on Good but is stepping up from a run base of 10f in most recent starts; the 26-day break matches Stintino Sunset's, trainer Marcus Tregoning sends daughter Alice (5lb claim) which keeps weight competitive, though the win column remains empty in current form.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a solid second three starts back, Little She arrives here on a sound 26-day break with experience over today's trip and a rating of 52 that edges above her official mark; the risk is that she has been winless in her last six starts and must prove she can convert.

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural style has been remapped here — form includes a win but recent runs show 6th, 5th, U, 4th, and 3rd, with the unstable profile compounded by a 7lb-claiming amateur in Mr Josh Myers and a course/trip combination (14f on Good) that produced a 6th-place finish historically; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags meaningful positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of mid-field finishes and an unseating in recent form, The Pug is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine rival to press her, she is expected to bowl along at a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset. Stintino Sunset and Little She will push forward from the prominent positions to track her, likely forming a compact group through the early stages, while Highland Harvey, Wrist Art, and the redistributed The Pug settle in behind. At Brighton's undulating track over this trip, a steady-to-moderate gallop set by an uncontested leader typically compresses the field and makes it difficult for hold-up horses to generate a meaningful finishing kick in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can comfortably place at the rear — The Pug is a genuine hold-up performer who has been remapped to midfield, but in practice may find that position hard to maintain cleanly. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers and the front-runner herself, as the lack of pace pressure and Brighton's punishing final climb reward those settled close to the lead with cover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Of Charm Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Charm leads unchallenged at a fair clip and the prominent horses cannot sustain their challenge up the hill.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Charm dictates from the front at a measured gallop, never coming under serious pressure, and the steady pace compresses the field to the point where her rivals lack room to build momentum; Good ground and her course-applicable form over similar trips consolidate the advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Stintino Sunset or Little She track Sea Of Charm closely enough to pounce in the final two furlongs when the leader ties.
scenarios.body: A modest tempo allows the two prominent horses to sit in a perfect striking position, and one of them edges ahead as Sea Of Charm fades under amateur handling late on; Good ground suits both, and their consistent placed form at this distance profile supports a finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up sufficiently through the middle stages to string out the field and create genuine late-run conditions.
scenarios.body: Highland Harvey, with the strongest recent form figures including a win and multiple places on Good ground, is the likeliest beneficiary as a genuine hold-up type capable of closing if gaps appear; Wrist Art is the secondary threat but lacks a win at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the race is disrupted by an uneven gallop, crowding on the undulating track, or amateur errors that scramble the field order.
scenarios.body: With six amateur jockeys of varying experience and a course that punishes positional mistakes, a breakdown in running order could allow an unexpected winner to emerge from any position; The Pug, forced wide of its natural role, is the most exposed horse if things unravel.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Charm — watch whether Mr Henry Main (3lb claimer, amateur) settles her comfortably in front without going too fast early; if she bowls along unchallenged the race is likely hers, but erratic pace-setting would open the door to the prominent horses.

Stintino Sunset and Little She — both race prominently and will contest the same ground just off Sea Of Charm's heels; if they crowd each other or one overreaches turning for home on Brighton's camber, both could lose their position at the critical moment.

The Pug — watch whether Josh Myers (7lb claimer) can hold the horse's natural hold-up inclination in a small, slowly run field; being shuffled wide or forced to race in an unnatural prominent position would cost it significantly.

Highland Harvey — the form horse on paper but entirely dependent on pace developing through the race; if Sea Of Charm dawdles and the field stays bunched, watch for McGaffin (5lb claim) attempting to move earlier than ideal to compensate.

Wrist Art — monitor the market move given the step up in trip; if there is support for a horse whose recent runs have been over 8–10f, that confidence may reflect connections believing the extra distance suits, which would make it a genuine each-way factor under Miss Ruby Criscuolo (5lb claim).

races.name: blackmorebuild.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cruse On Bye
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Michael Attwater whose best form came second at 6f on Good; James Glennon's 7lb claim is a material asset and the return to Good ground is a plus, though two runs without a win or place at 6f suggests a step up in consistency is needed.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Four starts have produced two placings at 5f on Good ground — specifically the surface and trip conditions today — and Abdulla Rashid Al-Hajri's 5lb claim helps offset the 69-day absence; travels prominently and should find this configuration sympathetic.

runners_data.name: Water Angel
runners_data.note: Ray Dawson takes the ride on this hold-up filly with just one run to her name — a fifth at 6f on Good — and Dylan Cunha's yard is in strong form (5/25 over 14 days); the lack of experience and the hold-up style on a track that doesn't easily reward late closers are the key factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's yard has been busy (3/32) and Marco Ghiani is a capable partner, but the horse's genuine hold-up profile means she is racing further forward than is natural here given the field's composition — six runs without a win and the positional compromise both temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Space Dreamer
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's unbeaten-in-the-making front-runner has been fresh (39 days off) and has two fifths to show, but the crucial point is that no other confirmed front-runner contests the lead; Billy Loughnane should enjoy a trouble-free rail on this tight-turning track and the Good surface is confirmed suitable.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides this hold-up filly who has raced only once on Good ground (1/5 in that going band) and returns from a 23-day break; James Owen's trainer strike rate is notable (7/41) but Tricky Jenny's record of consistent minor placing without winning reflects a horse that needs things to go wrong for others to win.

races.paceDynamic: Space Dreamer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Billy Loughnane should be able to dictate a controlled, metronomic gallop from the front over Brighton's unique undulating 5½f. The two prominent-style runners, Cruse On Bye and Tree Wizard, will press for position behind Space Dreamer but are unlikely to force a genuine pace war, meaning the tempo is likely to be honest rather than scorching. Last Dandelion, a true hold-up horse, has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field has more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate — Space Dreamer and, to a lesser extent, Cruse On Bye are best-placed to secure their natural positions, while Last Dandelion may find herself shuffled further back than ideal. On Good ground over this trip at Brighton, a settled single-pace gallop set by an uncontested leader favours a horse that can travel prominently and sustain its effort up the final climb, making the prominent-to-lead profile the most advantaged shape in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Space Dreamer Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Space Dreamer goes unchallenged to the lead and sets a comfortable, unforced tempo from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Loughnane dictates the fractions from his natural front-running berth, and with no rival forcing the issue the race becomes a test of who has the most horsepower in a controlled sprint home. Horses who have tracked the pace from a prominent position are ideally placed to challenge, while hold-up horses face too much ground to make up on a course that does not offer a dramatic late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cruse On Bye or Tree Wizard travel smoothly just off Space Dreamer and produce a decisive finishing effort up the hill.
scenarios.body: Space Dreamer's controlled pace keeps the race well within those horses' comfort zones, and a prominent tracker who handles Good ground can accelerate past the leader inside the final furlong. Tree Wizard's multiple placed efforts at 5f on Good going give it a specific scenario claim here if it secures a handy pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong, opening a gap for a closer to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Water Angel or Last Dandelion would need the early leaders to tie up from an overly generous early gallop — unlikely given Space Dreamer's uncontested lead — but Brighton's undulating finish can catch out front-runners who have burned too much energy. Last Dandelion is a true hold-up type racing out of her ideal position, which makes this scenario harder to execute and lowers its realistic probability accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Break Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If a poor or uneven start disrupts Space Dreamer or causes Cruse On Bye to lose ground, fundamentally reshaping the pace picture.
scenarios.body: With the single pace-setter compromised, the race becomes a rough-and-tumble sprint with no established rhythm, potentially playing into the hands of any horse that finds a clear run from an unexpected position. Tricky Jenny, with her consistent record of finding a place, could benefit from the chaos if she avoids trouble.

watchPoints.text: Space Dreamer and the draw: monitor whether Loughnane secures the rail cleanly at the start — any stumble or wide draw disadvantage could fundamentally alter the pace picture in this race.
Tree Wizard's 69-day absence after a busy juvenile campaign (four runs) means fitness cannot be assumed; watch the market move for evidence the Kobeissi team is happy with the horse's condition.
Last Dandelion has run just three days ago (LR:3d) which is an unusually short turnaround for a juvenile on an undulating track — monitor for any signs of fatigue or jockey adjustment mid-race.

Water Angel is lightly raced (one run) and Dylan Cunha's stable is firing at 5/25 over 14 days — an unexposed horse with a live stable angle could outrun her odds if she handles the Brighton undulations well on debut trip adjustment.

races.name: John Heal Memorial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dreams Galore
runners_data.note: Two wins from two attempts on Good ground, both front-running, both at this sort of trip — Ollie Sangster's filly is in the form of her life (W-W-W in last three including a 71-rated win 14 days ago) and Billy Loughnane simply needs to roll out of the gates and control this from the front.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive wins make Dreams Galore the one to beat here, and having run over today's trip and going she faces no unknowns on those fronts; drawn in stall two carrying 141 lb, the 71-rated filly returns on a handy 14-day turnaround in fine heart.

runners_data.name: Harry's Pop
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's yard is in strong form (5 wins from 25 over 14 days) and Ray Dawson picks up a live ride on a two-year-old who won last time at 6f on Good — a prominent style suits him ideally here and he maps perfectly to stalk Dreams Galore.
runners_data.comment: Harry's Pop won last time out and brings strong fitness into this, having run just six days ago, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; drawn in stall one carrying 141 lb, the main risk is whether his prior form figures suggest that consistency at this level.

runners_data.name: Cydney Sweenie
runners_data.note: 46 days off the track is the key query for this hold-up filly, and Jack Morland's yard has had zero winners in seven runs over the same period — Callum Shepherd will need a strong pace to be set to bring her home from the back.
runners_data.comment: Cydney Sweenie shaped with promise when third three starts back and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her firmly in the mix, but winless in her last four and returning after 46 days off, she needs to recapture that form sharply.

runners_data.name: Crowned
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just three runs and a style that is genuinely uncertain (U-style), Darragh Keenan inherits an unknown quantity — the form peak was a third at 5f on Good, but going up to 6f and matching more experienced rivals is asking plenty at this stage.
runners_data.comment: Crowned has been running respectably in recent starts, third three starts back and returning after just 18 days, with experience over today's trip adding to his claims; the risk is he remains yet to win in his last three outings.

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good earlier in the season but has been well beaten in five subsequent outings, and the trainer's 7/41 strike rate over 14 days suggests the yard is not firing at peak — Luke Morris tracks up prominently but the form figures suggest she is vulnerable.
runners_data.comment: Pageant Girl has struggled in her last four starts, finishing unplaced most recently and failing to trouble the judge across that sequence, and her speed rating leaves her short of what looks required here. Experience over today's trip and going offers some grounding, but it is hard to make a case on current form.

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: Wears a blinker for the first time today — worth noting as a significant gear change — but the hold-up style and a string of finishes in the 5-8 range make her reliant on something going wrong in front; Philip McBride's yard sends her here off 16 days rest with an OR of just 51.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fifth in five of them, Priscilla's Hope is hard to fancy from stall six on these figures, though she has distance and going experience and returns after a sharp 16-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Dreams Galore is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with only Harry's Pop and Pageant Girl likely to track up in behind from prominent positions, she faces no genuine pace pressure from rivals willing to match her stride for stride. On Good ground over 6f at Brighton — a track with a stiff uphill finish that tests stamina — she can dictate a controlled, honest tempo without being harried into setting a suicidal gallop. The hold-up horses Cydney Sweenie and Priscilla's Hope will need something to go wrong in front to land a telling blow, while the prominent pair behind Dreams Galore will be ideally placed if the pace eases. This race shape most clearly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — those who can track the leader into the straight and have enough left to outstay her up the hill.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dreams Galore Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Dreams Galore secures an uncontested lead and sets a sustainable pace that stretches the field on the climb.
scenarios.body: She dictates from the front, keeps the tempo honest rather than suicidal, and her rivals simply cannot get to her up the Brighton hill — her two wins on Good ground both came front-running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Harry's Pop or Pageant Girl track Dreams Galore closely and outstay her in the final furlong on the testing climb.
scenarios.body: One or both prominent horses sit just off the pace and, as Dreams Galore's effort flattens out late, the proximity advantage allows them to collar her without needing a dramatic finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Arrives Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to set up a stamina-sapping finish that brings hold-up horses into play.
scenarios.body: Cydney Sweenie or Priscilla's Hope, racing from deep, need Dreams Galore to have gone too hard early and the leaders to visibly tie up on the hill — a slim dependency given one uncontested front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically — a slow pace that collapses the field and produces an anything-can-happen sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Crowned or Priscilla's Hope, with nothing to lose at big prices, could benefit from total chaos but this requires multiple horses to run well below form simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Dreams Galore — watch whether Billy Loughnane settles her at a sustainable clip or goes too fast too soon; the difference between a controlled lead and a burned-out leader will define the entire race.
Priscilla's Hope — first-time blinkers are a significant addition and could alter her behaviour in the early stages, potentially changing her usual hold-up pattern if they sharpen her.
Harry's Pop — ran just 6 days ago; monitor any signs of fatigue late on the Brighton climb, as a quick turnaround can leave a horse flat in the final furlong.
Pageant Girl — her one win came at 6f on Good, matching today's conditions exactly, but five largely disappointing runs since suggest that may now be some way behind her current level.

races.name: Blackmore Equestrian Construction Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Final)

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: In sparkling recent form with three wins from her last five including back-to-back 7f victories on Good; drops to 6f here but handles it, and a hold-up style suits this pace-dominated shape perfectly — jockey Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a bonus.
runners_data.comment: Prefer The Sister won two starts back and is a mare who clearly knows how to win, with experience over today's trip and going in her favour; however, she carries 138 lb from stall 14 and our rating of 66 suggests she faces a stiff ask against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: One of the race's confirmed front-runners who will fight for the lead from the outset; has winning form on Good ground over 7f but faces a real test if he burns energy contesting early supremacy with Kento and Candy Warhol; trainer Wigham without a recent winner (0/5 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Dion Baker shaped well when third three starts back and a winner four starts back, and he arrives here fresh enough on 17 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the main concern is that a mark of 73 may leave him with something to find.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid 6f Good ground credentials — placed twice at this trip in similar conditions — and trainer Attwater has one winner from 13 runners in the past fortnight; 24 days off, returns fresh, and a fast pace suits his strong-finishing profile.
runners_data.comment: Twirler shaped well with a second last time out and her experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead; our rating puts her narrowly top of this 16-runner field, and 24 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough to go one better.

runners_data.name: Neptune Legend
runners_data.note: Lightly raced on Good ground (4/15 runs) but has two wins at 6f on Good or Firm; hold-up style suits a strong pace but David Egan faces a 16-runner puzzle and last six outings include several disappointing finishes; visor and tongue tie in use.
runners_data.comment: Neptune Legend won two starts back and boasts three wins in his last six, bringing solid recent form to the table; however, a sixth last time out, 31 days off the track, and a trainer running at just 5% in the past fortnight are genuine concerns for this 129 lb carry from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back races on Good ground at 6f and is freshest in the field at just 5 days since last run — Billy Loughnane is a big-race jockey and this hold-up type has shown he can finish quickly off a strong pace, though the step up in competitiveness is noted.
runners_data.comment: Arnaz arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid each-way claims at a competitive weight of 129 lb; the chief concern is that five days between runs leaves his recovery on the short side.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent, likely to sit just behind the front-running trio rather than contesting the lead itself; two recent wins on Good ground with visor fitted, and from this stalking position could prove the biggest danger if the leaders fall apart.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out and a winner three starts back, Secret Handsheikh arrives in decent nick on 18 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going, but a mixed recent profile — fifth and two out-of-the-money efforts in between — keeps him firmly in the each-way bracket from stall 10 off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been running consistently in the places over 7-8f on Good ground; drops in trip to 6f which may not fully suit his longer-striding style, and no wins from 15 runs in similar conditions is a concerning statistic in a wide-open field.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and second four starts back show Giant has threatened without converting, and his rating of 68 suggests he retains ability; but a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the past fortnight is the chief concern here.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner alongside Dion Baker; has placed repeatedly at 6f on Good including a win last time — the concern is how much energy is burned fighting for the lead; trainer Carroll with Ghiani up is a positive pairing but the pace battle is a significant risk.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has placed four times in his last six starts, with a win two starts further back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — but a trainer operating at just 5% in the past fortnight is a concern, and he is ranked ninth of sixteen on our assessment.

runners_data.name: Diomed Spirit
runners_data.note: Has genuine front-running or close-tracking form — his recent win came at 6f on Good — but with the pace map saturated, he is displaced into midfield and must race away from his natural position; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects a meaningful reduction in his expected effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Diomed Spirit won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid recent platform, but he carries 122 lb from stall six and his broader recent record shows inconsistency, with three sixth-place finishes in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: Prominent type with three wins from ten runs at 6f on Good, making him one of the best-qualified runners for this specific conditions profile; likely to sit just off the pace battle and could prove the value play if the front-runners tie each other up — solid 10/15 sim-going record.
runners_data.comment: Big Time Rascal arrives in fair heart on the back of a win last time out, and he was also a winner three starts back, but ranked 12 of 16 on our figures he faces a stiff task, with the fifth two starts back doing little to suggest consistency.

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner, though the weakest of the trio on recent form — no wins from three runs at 6f on Good or Standard and the simulated-going record is thin (3/15); at OR 53 and 7 years old, burning energy fighting for the lead looks a risky profile here.
runners_data.comment: Candy Warhol has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, yet remains winless in his last six starts. He has run over today's trip and going, carries 117 lb from stall seven, and 23 days between runs suggests he returns fresh enough to challenge again.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good just five runs ago and has placed repeatedly at this trip — a genuinely effective horse when allowed to race comfortably, but crammed into midfield by the volume of hold-up types, he will need to work against his nature; STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Washington Heir has shown some ability in recent starts — a winner three starts back, third two starts back, and second last time out — but he ranks fifteenth of sixteen on our figures and faces a stiff ask, with his trainer striking at just five per cent in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted and has a 6f Good ground win in his recent history, but the last five runs show a largely inconsistent profile; apprentice jockey Myla Coppins (5lb claim) is a factor, and like several stablemates, he is squeezed into a midfield slot that does not reflect how he ideally operates.
runners_data.comment: Port Hedland has finished eighth, fifth, and eighth in his last three starts, and although he scored four runs back, his overall recent profile is hard to ignore at the foot of the rankings; experience over today's trip and going offers some small comfort, but the trainer's 5% strike rate in the last 14 days compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good ground and has consistent placed form in similar conditions — the concern is that he is a natural hold-up horse displaced into midfield by race shape congestion, and Tyler Heard must navigate traffic on a horse that ideally needs a clear passage from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Bated Breeze won two starts back but has since finished fourth, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call on; the 114 lb burden and a stall-15 draw are the countervailing factors, though a rating of 58 suggests he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Inconsistent profile with no wins in recent similar-going conditions (0/1 in sim-going) and a form string featuring several disappointing efforts; at OR 45 in a 16-runner field, the combination of a compressed midfield position and modest recent form makes this a difficult winning proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a latest effort of eighth and little to recommend him on the figures — ranked bottom of the field — Daley T faces a stiff ask here, though he does have experience over today's trip and going, and 114 lb is a manageable weight.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with visor fitted and no wins from five runs in similar going — Olivia Haines (7lb claimer) takes the ride, which reduces the weight burden, but the form and style displacement into midfield combine to make this a very unlikely winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, My Boy Jack has little in his favour on our figures, ranked 13 of 16, though he has run over today's trip and going before and has a fitness edge at 28 days since his last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker, Kento, and Candy Warhol are all confirmed front-runners and will immediately contest for the early lead down Brighton's opening straight, guaranteeing a strong, honest gallop over this 6f on Good ground. With three genuine pace-setters fighting for the same real estate, this is not a scenario where one horse controls tempo and conserves energy — the early fractions will be genuinely quick, stretching the field and placing a premium on stamina and the ability to sustain effort into the sharp uphill finish Brighton demands. Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal are likely to land in the prominent group just behind the battling leaders, giving them a relatively handy position without having burned fuel fighting for the front. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can race off the honest gallop and produce a sustained late run, particularly those proven on Good ground over 6f at this track — the pace battle up front creates the ideal conditions for a well-tuned closer. The field contains significantly more true hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Diomed Spirit, Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Bated Breeze, Daley T, and My Boy Jack are genuine come-from-behind horses who will be shuffled into midfield positions rather than their natural ground-saving spots, meaning they will need to work harder than usual and their chances must be tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Dion Baker, Kento, and Candy Warhol burns each other out before halfway, leaving the field strung out and the front rank empty.
scenarios.body: The honest early fractions set by the trio of front-runners drain their reserves on the climb to the line, and the race opens up for horses who raced patiently behind the leaders in the prominent-to-midfield group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives Melee
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely Dion Baker or Kento — establishes a fractional lead and dictates at a controlled enough tempo to hold on.
scenarios.body: Rather than a burning three-abreast battle, one runner gets a clear toe and the others are unable to match them stride-for-stride, allowing the leader to ration their effort into the final climb.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle neutralises all three leaders and the race is won from just off the pace by a horse who tracked the leaders without expending early energy.
scenarios.body: Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal, both proven at 6f on Good ground and natural prominent types, are best placed to exploit a leader implosion without needing to come from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Deep Closer Defies Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce and the field so strung out that a true hold-up horse manages to pick through traffic despite racing out of its natural position.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given the volume of redistributed hold-up types crowding the midfield — Washington Heir, Diomed Spirit, and Bated Breeze all face a harder task than usual and must navigate significant traffic on top of an already-compressed rear.

watchPoints.text: If Dion Baker, Kento, and Candy Warhol race three-abreast from the off, watch for any one of them weakening sharply inside the final 2f and causing interference as the field fans out on Brighton's unique undulating straight.

Prefer The Sister and Arnaz are the hold-up horses best equipped to exploit the expected pace collapse — watch whether their jockeys get a clean passage through the 16-runner field approaching the final climb.
Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal are the prominent types most likely to benefit from the pace battle — watch whether they can maintain position without being sucked into the early tempo war.

Tony Carroll has four runners in this race (Neptune Legend, Kento, Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Daley T) which may create tactical complications — watch whether any of the stablemates are ridden to assist another runner or interfere with each other's racing room.

Brighton's uphill finish from the 2f pole is a significant stamina test at the end of a truly run 6f — watch for horses that are prominent at the 2f pole but clearly tying up on the climb, as the finishing positions can change dramatically in the final 100 yards.

races.name: Blackmore Design & Build Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Won twice over 7f on Good ground and returns just 18 days after a runner-up effort, bringing clear course-distance form and the significant tactical advantage of being the only natural pace-setter in this field; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps offset the 137lbs, and the sole-lead scenario is highly compatible with her best form, though she maps slightly out of her sharpest role as a true front-runner here.
runners_data.comment: Sea Suite arrives here in fine nick, winning last time out and a close second two starts back, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; the 137 lb burden is the one query, but he looks primed at 18 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Knights Gold
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over for Tom Ward, whose recent 14-day strike rate of 1/15 is modest, but Knights Gold has placed five times in his last nine runs and his two hits at 8f on Good suggest he stays well; a genuine hold-up type who will need Sea Suite to set a strong enough pace to reel in over the final 2f.
runners_data.comment: Knights Gold has been consistently competitive in recent starts, finishing third or better on three occasions in his last six, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that he remains yet to win in this recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Foreseen
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll saddles this 5-year-old who won last time over 8f on Good and steps down slightly in trip, which should sharpen his finishing effort; a natural hold-up horse who has placed three times from hold-up positions on similar-going surfaces, though the controlled pace Sea Suite is likely to set makes his task harder than the form book alone suggests.
runners_data.comment: Foreseen won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 88 makes him a clear threat from stall three on a quick turnaround; the main concern is a trainer who has sent out just one winner from 20 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: David Egan takes a horse who has recorded zero wins or places on similar going in his five recent runs, and his form string of 864080 makes grim reading regardless of pace shape; though he is a true hold-up type by nature, the map has him in midfield — and even if he gets closer to the pace, nothing in his recent profile suggests he can capitalise on it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dapper Guest yet to show his best form of late, though he has run over today's distance and going before and comes here fresh on just 11 days' rest; our rating of 80 suggests a shade more ability than his official mark of 76 implies.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Two places over 7f on Good in his last five runs gives North View more course-trip-going credentials than several rivals, and Luke Morris is an experienced navigator of Brighton's quirky layout; a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map — his best chance comes only if Sea Suite burns them off mid-race and he can pick up the pieces, which is the least probable scenario here.
runners_data.comment: North View has placed in two of his last three starts — third last time out and a second two starts back — and has run over today's distance and going before, returning after just 17 days in good order; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 5% in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: A 59-day break is a notable flag, and Patrick Chamings' 14-day record of 0/9 offers little trainer confidence for the return; her five recent runs have all been over 5-6f, making this 7f trip a genuine stamina question, and while she has placed on Good ground, the combination of the layoff, step up in distance, and hold-up style in a slowly-run race makes her profile the hardest to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Cuban Lady faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before and a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort after a lengthy 59-day absence.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: Three wins over 7f on Good in his last five eligible runs is a standout statistic, and the tp headgear suggests connections are trying to sharpen his focus; a true hold-up horse by nature — redistributed forward on the map — who is 9 days fresh and carries the lowest weight in the field at 120lbs, making him a value-angle closer if any late chaos materialises, though the controlled gallop Sea Suite is likely to set is his principal obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures, King Of War has finished eighth and unplaced in his last two starts, and though he did win five starts back, that form has dried up considerably since, making him very hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and distance and a quick nine-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Suite is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to push her along, meaning she can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over Brighton's undulating 7f. The rest of the field — Knights Gold, Foreseen, Dapper Guest, North View, Cuban Lady, and King Of War — are all hold-up types by nature, leaving Sea Suite to effectively control every fraction from the front. With no pressure expected early, she is likely to bowl along at a tempo that suits herself rather than the closers, and on Good ground at a track that rewards those who travel strongly into the straight, the race shape firmly favours the prominent racer who can dictate and quicken. Note: the field contains significantly more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically be accommodated at the rear — Dapper Guest, North View, Cuban Lady, and King Of War are all true late-closers redistributed to midfield on the map, and with Sea Suite setting a controlled pace, they face the twin problem of racing without their ideal late surge and finding a gap in a compressed, slowly-run field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Suite Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite breaks well and sets an uncontested, measured gallop with no rivals willing or able to challenge for the lead.
scenarios.body: Sea Suite dictates every fraction on her own terms over Brighton's 7f, quickening before the final turn and putting the race to bed before the hold-up horses can organise their challenges; the prominent-racing profile is the clear beneficiary when the pace is a sole-conductor affair on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite sets a falsely slow tempo that leaves the field bunched and a wall of hold-up horses able to produce one late coordinated surge.
scenarios.body: With the pace overly modest, the closers get a fair test despite their redistributed positions, and the Better-handicapped hold-up types can close ground rapidly in the final furlong; Knights Gold and Foreseen, the two most consistent hold-up performers with solid form on Good ground, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race, Hold-Ups Caught
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite injects a strong middle sectional that stretches the field and leaves the true hold-up runners chasing shadows from too far back.
scenarios.body: A genuine mid-race injection of pace turns this into a test of stamina and positional quality, ruthlessly exposing those redistributed hold-up horses who cannot get into striking position early enough; Sea Suite and whoever tracks her most closely into the straight hold the decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Hands It To Foreseen
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched, hold-up-dominated field creates significant interference in the straight and only one horse finds clear daylight early.
scenarios.body: Foreseen, with Tony Carroll's record of placing horses to peak sharply and a recent win on Good ground at a similar trip, could be the one to slip through a gap if the field stalls momentarily; King Of War's three wins at 7f on Good also makes him a live outsider if the race degenerates into a lottery.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sea Suite breaks cleanly and immediately controls the pace — if she misses the break or is pushed wide early, the entire dominant scenario collapses and the hold-up horses gain a crucial length of momentum.

Monitor Dapper Guest's position in running: if David Egan cannot improve on a form string of 864080 despite a good draw, he becomes a significant traffic hazard in a field of seven that is bunched in midfield.

Cuban Lady's 59-day absence and step up from 6f to 7f is a dual unknown — if she fades badly in the straight she could obstruct the hold-up closers arriving late, particularly Knights Gold and Foreseen.

King Of War's 120lb bottom weight gives J F Egan a fitness edge in a compact field — watch whether he can position closer than his natural hold-up style suggests, given the redistribution of so many rivals to his preferred patch of track.

North View has placed twice over 7f on Good recently for Luke Morris at Brighton — if Sea Suite's pace is genuinely modest rather than controlled, he is the hold-up horse most likely to bridge the gap given his proven course-trip-going profile.

races.name: Blackmore Proudly Sponsoring Brighton Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Marsh Benham
runners_data.note: Two wins and three places from 15 runs on similar going, including two wins over course and distance, make this seven-year-old's form profile compelling, but Benoit de la Sayette must generate momentum from the rear with just five runners — a slow solo pace from Danehill Star shrinks the advantage for a natural hold-up horse.|
runners_data.comment: Marsh Benham won two starts back and was runner-up three starts back, giving him a sharp recent profile, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the concern is last time's sixth just two days ago, though draw four and a solid weight of 140 lb suit a horse in this form.

runners_data.name: War Chant
runners_data.note: Callum Shepherd rides a horse who has shaped as a prominent racer in recent starts, and a headgear flag (p) flags a potential switch in tactics; only one win from five on similar going but the trainer's 2/15 14-day form suggests modest current yard form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, War Chant nevertheless rates the pick of this field on our figures and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that his form line shows a persistent inability to convert.

runners_data.name: Nordic Norm
runners_data.note: A 72-day absence is the headline concern, and a zero win-zero place record from two runs on similar going compounds the doubt; the tongue-tie flag (t) is worth noting, but J.R. Jenkins's 1/4 14-day record gives slim encouragement that the yard has this horse ready.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed effort three starts back gives Nordic Norm a solid foundation, and he has experience of today's trip and going; carrying 137 lb from stall 3, the main concern is that he arrives on the back of two below-par efforts and is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on this trip and going combination underline genuine ability, and Gary & Moore's 2/16 14-day record is solid; however, this horse's natural instinct is to race held up, and mapped to midfield due to the congestion of hold-up types, the style-fit flag (0.94) signals it may not get its ideal position — discount its chance marginally in a shape built around a steady pace.|
runners_data.comment: My Old Mate arrives in fine heart, a winner two starts back and a winner three starts back, and he shaped well for third last time out; he has run over today's trip and carries a workable 131 lb from stall five, though a return to form after just five days is the key question.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's veteran leads every scenario by default with no rivals capable of or likely to match his desire to front-run; David Egan's experience on Brighton's tricky course is an asset, and seven places from fifteen runs on Good going confirm he is at home under these conditions — a 0/20 trainer 14-day record is the one material concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Danehill Star also has the headwind of a trainer in poor recent form (1/20 over the last 14 days); experience over today's trip and going, plus draw one, offer thin consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Danehill Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press him, David Egan can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Brighton's undulating mile. War Chant is the only prominent-style horse and will likely track Danehill Star in second, meaning the pace is set by one horse rather than a contest of wills — a measured tempo is the almost certain outcome. My Old Mate is a genuine hold-up type who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate all hold-up runners at the rear, but in practice Billy Loughnane may well find him further back than the map suggests; Marsh Benham and Nordic Norm are also natural hold-up horses who will genuinely be hunting from the rear. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner and any horse with the tactical versatility to sit close to the pace, as a steady, uncontested gallop will make life hard for true closers trying to generate enough momentum from off the pace on Good turf at Brighton.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danehill Star Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Danehill Star leads at a measured tempo and War Chant settles comfortably in second without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Egan dictates every fraction, the pace stays honest but not searching, and the hold-up horses — Marsh Benham, Nordic Norm, My Old Mate — are left needing a finishing burst that a slow pace never generates; Danehill Star's consistent placed record on Good ground over this trip makes him the principal beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: War Chant Presses Hard
scenarios.trigger: If Callum Shepherd sends War Chant forward to press Danehill Star and creates a genuinely contested pace.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop opens the race up and gives horses coming from off the pace a real target to close down in the final two furlongs; War Chant's form in similar-going races and recent trainer strike rate give him claims if he can exploit the pace scenario he helps to create.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely strong enough to compromise the leaders and My Old Mate or Marsh Benham can produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: My Old Mate has back-to-back wins on this trip and going combination and, if racing from a genuinely held-up position further back than his mapped slot, could arrive late with a clean run; Marsh Benham's two recent wins over this identical course and distance configuration make him the other viable finisher in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Nordic Norm Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If Nordic Norm overcomes 72 days off and a modest similar-going record to produce a career-best effort from hold-up.
scenarios.body: A big layoff and a record of zero wins or places on comparable ground makes this an outsider scenario that relies on the Jenkins-trained gelding having improved markedly since his last run; he would need every other horse to underperform.

watchPoints.text: Danehill Star is the only confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field — if Egan finds no pressure whatsoever he could set a dawdle that turns this into a sprint, which would compress the finishing order and make the race far harder to read.|

My Old Mate's 5-day turnaround is short and, if Loughnane cannot position him in a comfortable spot given the crowded hold-up end of the field, his ability to produce his best form is compromised — watch the early-race positioning closely.|

War Chant's headgear flag (p) suggests connections may be trying something different tactically; if Shepherd elects to press Danehill Star hard early rather than settle, the entire race shape changes from a solo-led dawdle to a genuinely contested pace.|

Nordic Norm has not run for 72 days and has no wins or places on similar going — monitor market moves in the final hour, as any significant support would suggest stable confidence that is not visible in the public form record.|
